messages.subject: Shrinking Fonts
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I'm using JGR to teach and have set the font size to 22 so students in the back can read it. However, when I submit the code, it shows up tiny. I've done this with previous versions and the fonts stayed large. I've tried both Edit> Preferences and CTRL+Sh+I and get the same result. I just loaded the latest version of Java and reinstalled JGR but that didn't help. Any ideas?

Thanks,
Bob

messages.subject: Re: Problems assigning a REXP to a variable
messages.subject_clean: Problems assigning a REXP to a variable
messages.body_plain:
More on that, how can I know if a specific REXP is not supported by Rserve?
In your answer you talk about ENVSXP. How can I prevent my system to
run any of these not allowed operations? The received REXP from the lm
function is a REXPGenericVector that looks fine to me.

In other words, which comparison should I do with the REXP to decide
that it will make the system fail?

Thanks again!

    Víctor


On Fri, Sep 28, 2012 at 5:42 PM, Simon Urbanek
<simon.urbanek at r-project.org> wrote:
> On Sep 28, 2012, at 10:52 AM, Víctor Pascual Cid wrote:
>
>> Hi there,
>>
>> I've found a possible bug when trying to assign the REXP that produces the execution of a linear model to a variable. This is the code:
>>
>> RConnection c = new RConnection();
>> REXP rexp = c.eval("linear_model <-lm(c(4,4,4,5)~c(18, 14, 12, 18)+c(7,6,1,6)+c(37, 27, 32, 57))");
>> c.assign("myVar", rexp);
>>
>> The execution of the last line produces the following error:
>>
>> *** REXPFactory unable to interpret org.rosuda.REngine.REXPUnknown@76539f0d[4]
>> org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: assign failed
>>       at org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection.assign(RConnection.java:285)
>>
>> It looks like the REXP generated with the output of the lm function is not recognized by the system itself.
>
> This is not a bug, 4 = ENVSXP and those are not supported by Rserve because they are reference-semantics objects, so they cannot be passed by value. They are only supported in JRI which has a notion of references.
>
> In addition, note that assign() supports only a subset of REXPs, it is only intended for vectors or lists that have been constructed in Java.
>
>
>> If I do execute a simple function such as "2+2" the code above works.
>>
>> Is there any workaround to prevent this kind of error?
>>
>
> Either assign it in R:
>
> c.voidEval("myVar <- linear_model <-lm(c(4,4,4,5)~c(18, 14, 12, 18)+c(7,6,1,6)+c(37, 27, 32, 57))");
>
> or use serialization. However, in that case you won't get exactly the same result because the environment will be copied and thus different from the environment of the original model (whether it matters or not depends on your application ...).
>
> Cheers,
> Simon
>
